description: The sufficient declaration, and the contrast to jcs-n-assembled-01. The same construction with a member mapping declared: each selected source path is pinned to its pre-image member name and nesting, and the one member that is not a source field is declared as a constant. Exactly one pre-image is derivable from the source object under this declaration, so the fork in jcs-n-assembled-01 is closed. The derivation is executed by the suite (Category J), not asserted in prose.
spec_ref: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §4 (derived identifier) and §13.2 (Artifact Type Registry digest context)

declared_digest_context.field_set: the source paths named in member_mapping.fields, and nothing else

note: `input` is the assembled object, which is what CANONICAL-DIGEST is applied to; `member_mapping` is what makes that object recoverable from `source_object` by a second implementer holding only the registry entry. Category J in check_vectors.py applies the mapping to `source_object` and asserts the result equals `input` exactly, so a mapping naming a path the source does not have, or producing a different object, is a hard failure rather than unread prose. The mapping closes both ambiguities the pair exercises. Re-keying: `_meta.binding` is pinned to the pre-image member `bindingBlock`, so implementation_a of jcs-n-assembled-01, which used `binding`, is no longer a conforming reading. Non-source members: `preimageRule` is declared as a constant, so a member that is not a source field at all is stated rather than discovered in a reference checker's source. `trace` is absent from the mapping and therefore absent from the pre-image, which is ordinary selection and needs no exclusion set.
shape_note: Two properties worth keeping if the shape changes. The mapping is a function from source paths to pre-image paths, so applying it to a source object yields exactly one assembled object and a checker can derive rather than trust it. And a context whose pre-image is the source object minus an exclusion set should declare `member_mapping: none` explicitly rather than omitting it, so a reader cannot mistake absence for a default. That second property matches the rule proposed for the §13.2 template in PR #9 — 'A registry entry is read in isolation by a verifier that has not read this document's prose, and cannot assume a default for an absent element' — which is not in main at the time of writing. If PR #9 does not land, this declaration shape needs its own statement of the same rule.
sequencing_note: This vector is written against the PR #9 registry template: `purpose` labels and `profile_version` are PR #9 elements, not main. `member_mapping` is in neither main nor PR #9; it is what this pair proposes.
